$comment: Shared cases for 'is this maxPagesForClassification a page limit?', exercised on
BOTH sides: by vitest against `isPageLimit` in ../classification-config.ts, and by
WHY A SHARED TABLE AND NOT TWO SUITES. The TypeScript predicate exists to tell an
operator importing an old file what the conversion will do to it, so the only thing
that makes it useful is agreeing with the Python one. The parity test beside it
compares the two VALUE LISTS by reading the TypeScript with a regex, which cannot see
a semantic divergence -- and one had already happened: the TypeScript stringified its
input before testing it, so an unquoted `2.5` answered false while Python truncates it
to a two-page limit and performs the conversion. The dialog said nothing and boundary
`json` holds the value as it arrives from a parsed JSON/YAML document, so a bare
number here is a real number on both sides. `limit` is what both predicates must
answer. Add a case here rather than to either suite.

cases.why: surrounding space is not a value
a real number is truncated: two pages
a fraction below one page is not a page count
a STRING must already spell a whole number; int('2.5') raises in Python
a boolean is not a page count, in either language
